To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rats avoid lick-contingent stimulation of the NST that mimics the temporal pattern of the taste response, and this temporal coding is specific for the taste stimulus that is paired with the stimulation.
rats avoided licking when the temporal pattern (number of pulses per second) of electrical stimulation mimicked a taste quality.
rats avoid electrical stimulation of the gustatory brainstem when the temporal pattern mimics the temporal pattern of taste responses to the tastants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of temporal coding of sensation in the neural control of behavior.
the neural mechanisms that underlie taste perception and taste-guided behavior.
the role of temporal coding of taste quality in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
temporal coding of sensation does not occur in the brain.
the temporal patterns of brain activity are important for taste perception and taste quality coding.
temporal coding of taste sensation in the brain is possible, but the exact mechanism is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
taste quality is represented by the temporal pattern of neural activity in the brain.
taste quality is coded in the brain by a combination of temporal and spatial patterns of neural activity.
temporal pattern coding in the brain can be learned and generalized to other tastants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal pattern can convey information about the quality of the tastant.
temporal pattern can convey information that is meaningful to the organism.
taste quality is not encoded solely by the identity of the taste cell type activated but also by the temporal patterning of the response.
